domain: {'name': 'Fact Verification with Multi-Hop Retrieval', 'content_type': 'Claim verification summaries and reasoning over Wikipedia passages', 'task_complexity': 'Requires tracing complex multi-entity relationships across multiple retrieval hops, identifying missing evidence, and determining when passages are insufficient for verification'}
summary: Failure modes generated and agreement-checked from 60 traces.

codes.name: Execution_Timeout
codes.description: Agent execution exceeded allocated time limit and was forcibly terminated before task completion.
codes.when_to_use: When agent process is killed or stopped due to exceeding time constraints, regardless of task progress.
codes.when_not_to_use: When agent completes execution within time limits but produces incomplete output for other reasons (use A.5).

codes.name: Multi_Hop_Context_Degradation
codes.description: Agent loses track of information, reasoning chains, or evidence from earlier retrieval iterations as the multi-hop loop progresses, failing to maintain coherent connections across the full reasoning trajectory.
codes.when_to_use: When agent demonstrates awareness of early-stage information initially but progressively loses connection to it in later iterations of a multi-hop retrieval task.
codes.when_not_to_use: When information loss happens immediately (use A.7). When context overflow prevents initial processing (use A.2). When single-hop task shows no multi-iteration component.

codes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
codes.description: External retrieval system provides passages that are insufficient in quantity, relevance, or quality, or fails to retrieve critical evidence needed for claim verification, through no fault of the agent.
codes.when_to_use: When the root cause of failure is poor retrieval quality, not agent processing. The agent cannot succeed because necessary evidence was never provided by upstream retrieval.
codes.when_not_to_use: When relevant evidence was retrieved but agent failed to use it (use A.7 or appropriate B/C code). When agent's poor query generation caused bad retrieval (use B code).

codes.name: Resource_Exhaustion
codes.description: Agent exceeded available computational resources (memory, context window, or processing capacity), causing execution failure or information loss.
codes.when_to_use: When agent fails due to insufficient memory, context capacity overflow, or other resource constraints that prevent normal processing.
codes.when_not_to_use: When agent completes execution but output is truncated for token generation limits (use A.5). When timeout occurs without resource exhaustion (use A.1).

codes.name: Generic_Execution_Error
codes.description: Agent encountered an unspecified system-level error during execution that prevented normal task completion.
codes.when_to_use: When agent fails due to infrastructure issues, runtime errors, or system problems that don't fit other specific categories.
codes.when_not_to_use: When failure has a specific identifiable cause covered by other codes (timeout, memory, parsing, etc.).

codes.name: Task_Refusal
codes.description: Agent explicitly declined to perform the assigned task, abandoned the task prematurely, or refused to provide required output.
codes.when_to_use: When agent consciously chooses not to complete the task, states it cannot or will not perform the work, or exits before completion by design rather than error.
codes.when_not_to_use: When agent attempts the task but fails due to technical limitations (use appropriate technical failure code).

codes.name: Output_Truncation
codes.description: Agent output was cut off during generation due to token limits or generation constraints, resulting in incomplete, partial, or entirely missing deliverables.
codes.when_to_use: When output generation stops prematurely due to length limits, producing incomplete content ranging from partial responses to completely empty output.
codes.when_not_to_use: When output is complete but wrong (use B/C codes). When truncation is due to timeout (use A.1) or resource exhaustion (use A.2).

codes.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
codes.description: Agent produces repetitive content, circularly restating the same information without progressing toward task completion.
codes.when_to_use: When output contains redundant cycles of the same content, phrases, or reasoning steps that don't advance task objectives.
codes.when_not_to_use: When repetition is intentional for emphasis or summary purposes. When agent is iterating through different items (not repeating same item).

codes.name: Upstream_Information_Loss
codes.description: Critical information from upstream sources (retrieval system, instructions, or prior processing stages) failed to reach, be processed, or be retained by the agent during task execution.
codes.when_to_use: When essential input information is available in the pipeline but doesn't manifest in agent processing, reasoning, or output despite being necessary for task completion.
codes.when_not_to_use: When information is genuinely absent from retrieval (use A.16). When loss is due to context overflow (use A.2). When loss occurs gradually in multi-hop reasoning (use A.11).

codes.name: Downstream_Handoff_Failure
codes.description: Agent output lacks critical information, proper structure, or necessary formatting required by downstream systems (retrieval loops, parsers, or next-stage agents) to continue processing, breaking the task pipeline.
codes.when_to_use: When agent produces output that cannot be successfully consumed by the next stage of processing, whether due to missing content, structural problems, or format violations.
codes.when_not_to_use: When output is structurally valid but semantically incorrect (use B/C codes). When truncation prevents completion (use A.5 as root cause).

codes.name: Inconsistent_Instruction_Set
codes.description: Agent receives significantly different instruction sets, prompts, or configurations across task instances, causing unpredictable behavior, variable output quality, or incomplete analysis due to guidance variability.
codes.when_to_use: When the same agent role receives different instructions for similar tasks, creating systematic inconsistency in how tasks are approached or evaluated.
codes.when_not_to_use: When instruction variation is intentional for different task types. When inconsistency is in agent behavior rather than instructions received (use appropriate B/C code).

codes.name: Coordinator_Unclear_Task_Specification
codes.description: Coordinator provides ambiguous, inconsistent, or incomplete task specifications that prevent precise execution. This includes varying instructions across invocations, ambiguous references, unclear entity boundaries, vague phrasing, or incomplete requirement statements.
codes.when_to_use: When the coordinator's task specification or claim presentation lacks the clarity needed for systematic verification
codes.when_not_to_use: When the coordinator provides clear specifications but other components fail to execute properly

codes.name: Solver_Insufficient_Evidence_Analysis
codes.description: Solver produces a verification conclusion without thoroughly analyzing whether provided passages contain sufficient evidence. This includes failing to identify missing evidence, not recognizing evidence gaps, or not explicitly stating when passages lack critical information needed for claim verification.
codes.when_to_use: When solver concludes verification without adequately assessing evidence completeness or identifying what information is missing
codes.when_not_to_use: When solver correctly identifies evidence gaps but coordinator fails to act on that identification

codes.name: Solver_Premature_Verification_Conclusion
codes.description: Solver renders definitive verification verdict (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) despite having incomplete evidence that cannot establish all claim components. This includes cases where only a subset of claim components are verified while other parts remain unaddressed or unverified.
codes.when_to_use: When solver provides definitive verdict without complete evidence coverage of all claim elements
codes.when_not_to_use: When solver appropriately indicates uncertainty or insufficient evidence (use B.2 instead)

codes.name: Coordinator_Compound_Claim_Without_Decomposition
codes.description: Coordinator provides multi-part claim requiring verification of multiple independent facts but does not structure it to guide systematic decomposition or verification of each component.
codes.when_to_use: When coordinator presents complex claims without providing structure for systematic verification
codes.when_not_to_use: When claim is genuinely atomic (single verifiable fact) or when decomposition guidance is present

codes.name: Coordinator_Vague_Retrieval_Guidance
codes.description: Coordinator provides vague or unclear guidance for retrieval operations. This includes using pronouns, implicit references, vague descriptions, or failing to specify explicit entity names and key concepts needed for effective information retrieval.
codes.when_to_use: When coordinator's retrieval instructions lack specificity needed for targeted information gathering
codes.when_not_to_use: When retrieval guidance is clear but retrieval system itself fails

codes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
codes.description: Incorrect interpretation or misreading of factual content explicitly stated in passages. This includes claiming a passage says X when it actually says Y, misattributing information, or incorrectly extracting facts from clear text.
codes.when_to_use: When solver demonstrably misinterprets clear, explicit passage content
codes.when_not_to_use: When passage content is genuinely ambiguous or when solver makes logical inference errors (not reading errors)

codes.name: Solver_Contradictory_Evidence_Not_Detected
codes.description: Failure to identify when passage evidence directly contradicts the claim. The reasoning does not recognize or highlight conflicts between claim statements and passage facts, potentially leading to incorrect SUPPORTS verdict.
codes.when_to_use: When passages contain clear contradictions to claim but solver does not flag them
codes.when_not_to_use: When contradiction is subtle or requires complex inference, or when passages are ambiguous

codes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
codes.description: Excessive analysis or reasoning about passages that are clearly irrelevant to the claim, diverting attention from relevant evidence or missing evidence gaps. Resources spent on tangential content rather than focused verification.
codes.when_to_use: When solver spends disproportionate effort analyzing clearly off-topic passages
codes.when_not_to_use: When initial relevance assessment is needed, or when passages have subtle relevance

codes.name: Coordinator_Premature_Hop_Termination
codes.description: Stopping the retrieval chain before completing all required hops in a multi-hop task. The reasoning concludes verification without requesting or analyzing all necessary information sources required by the task structure.
codes.when_to_use: When coordinator stops retrieval process before all necessary hops are completed
codes.when_not_to_use: When early stopping is appropriate due to definitive evidence or clear contradiction found

codes.name: Broken_Multi_Hop_Chain
codes.description: Failure to maintain logical continuity across multiple inference steps, where intermediate entities or relationships are skipped or not properly connected. The reasoning jumps to a conclusion without tracing through all necessary intermediate steps.
codes.when_to_use: When the claim requires reasoning through A→B→C→D but the trace jumps from A→D without establishing B or C, or when intermediate entity connections are asserted without evidence.
codes.when_not_to_use: When all hops are attempted but evidence is missing (use C.4). Do not use for single-hop reasoning failures or when the chain is complete but contains factual errors.

codes.name: Conditional_Reasoning_Error
codes.description: Errors in reasoning about conditional statements (if-then relationships), including affirming the consequent (if P then Q, Q is true, therefore P is true), denying the antecedent (if P then Q, P is false, therefore Q is false), or confusing necessary vs. sufficient conditions.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the claim or verification involves if-then logic and the reasoning commits conditional reasoning fallacies. Use when necessary conditions are treated as sufficient or vice versa. Use when converse or inverse is incorrectly assumed.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for general logical errors without conditional structure (use C.6). Do not use for claim decomposition of non-conditional compounds (use C.3).

codes.name: Set_Membership_Error
codes.description: Errors in reasoning about set membership, subset relationships, or category inclusion. This includes incorrectly determining whether an entity belongs to a category, whether one category is a subset of another, or confusion about overlapping vs. disjoint sets.
codes.when_to_use: Use when reasoning about 'X is a type of Y', 'X belongs to category Y', 'all X are Y', or 'some X are Y' is incorrect. Use when hierarchical category relationships are mishandled. Use when set operations (union, intersection) are incorrectly applied.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for universal/existential quantification errors (use C.2). Do not use when the category itself is correctly identified but attributes are wrong. Do not use for entity coreference (use C.15).

codes.name: Causal_Reasoning_Error
codes.description: Errors in reasoning about causation, including confusing correlation with causation, reversing cause and effect, assuming causation without evidence, or misidentifying causal chains. This includes temporal precedence confusion (post hoc ergo propter hoc) and confounding variable neglect.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the claim involves causal relationships ('X caused Y', 'because of X', 'led to', 'resulted in') and the reasoning incorrectly establishes or refutes causation. Use when correlation is treated as causation or when causal direction is reversed.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for temporal sequencing errors without causal claims (use C.8). Do not use for logical implication (use C.6 or C.11). Do not use when causation is not part of the claim.

codes.name: Existential_Universal_Confusion
codes.description: Confusion between existential claims (there exists at least one...) and universal claims (all/every/none...), or between specific and general statements.
codes.when_to_use: When claim requires showing X is true for all cases but reasoning only checks one instance, or when claim is about a specific instance but reasoning treats it as general statement.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the quantifier scope is correctly identified but other reasoning errors occur.

codes.name: Claim_Decomposition_Error
codes.description: Incorrect logical decomposition of compound or complex claims into verification sub-tasks. This includes treating conjunctions as disjunctions, missing conditional relationships, or incorrectly structuring the verification logic.
codes.when_to_use: When claim structure is 'A AND B' but reasoning treats it as 'A OR B', or when claim has conditional structure 'if A then B' but this logic is not preserved in verification approach.
codes.when_not_to_use: When decomposition is correct but individual components are checked incorrectly (use other codes for those specific errors).

codes.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
codes.description: Solver makes logical errors in connecting evidence to claim, including invalid inferences, contradictory reasoning steps, or failure to properly chain multi-hop evidence.
codes.when_to_use: When reasoning contains logical fallacies, contradictory statements, invalid inference steps, or fails to properly construct the reasoning chain from evidence to conclusion despite having sufficient passages.
codes.when_not_to_use: When evidence is insufficient (use Solver_B.1). This is about incorrect logical processing of available evidence, not missing evidence.

codes.name: Work_Author_Attribution_Confusion
codes.description: Confusion between a creative work and its creator, such as treating a book title as an author name or vice versa. This includes treating 'author of X' as equivalent to 'X the author'.
codes.when_to_use: When reasoning treats a work title (book, film, novel) as a person or treats an author as the work itself.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the work-creator relationship is correctly understood even if other errors exist.

codes.name: Temporal_Calculation_Error
codes.description: Incorrect calculation or comparison of dates, time periods, or temporal relationships. This includes arithmetic errors in computing year differences, incorrect direction of 'before/after' relationships, or wrong ordering of events.
codes.when_to_use: When reasoning performs explicit date arithmetic or temporal comparisons that are mathematically incorrect.
codes.when_not_to_use: When temporal information is missing from passages (that's C.4) rather than miscalculated.

codes.name: Entity_Coreference_Error
codes.description: Failure to correctly identify when different references, descriptions, or mentions refer to the same entity (under-merging), or incorrectly treating distinct entities as the same (over-merging). This includes failures in resolving pronouns, aliases, abbreviated names, descriptive references, or contextual mentions to their referent entities.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the trace shows failure to recognize that two different descriptions refer to the same entity (e.g., 'John Smith' and 'Smith' and 'he' not recognized as coreferent). Use when distinct entities are incorrectly merged (e.g., two different people with the same surname treated as one person). Use when contextual references are not resolved.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for simple entity misidentification without coreference involved. Do not use for work/author confusion (use C.7). Do not use when entity boundaries are correctly identified but attributes are wrong.

codes.name: Comparative_Reasoning_Error
codes.description: Errors in comparing entities along quantitative or qualitative dimensions, including incorrect magnitude comparisons (greater/less than), ranking errors, superlative determination failures (highest/lowest/first/last), or incorrect relative judgments. This includes having correct values but drawing wrong comparative conclusions.
codes.when_to_use: Use when entities are correctly identified with correct attribute values, but the comparison between them is incorrectly executed. Use when reasoning about 'more than', 'less than', 'taller', 'older', 'earliest', 'most', etc. is flawed despite having the necessary information.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the values being compared are themselves incorrect (that's a factual error). Do not use for temporal calculations (use C.8). Do not use when comparison logic is correct but applied to wrong entities (use C.15).

codes.name: Negation_Handling_Error
codes.description: Incorrect processing of negation in claims or evidence, including treating negative statements as positive, failing to recognize negation scope, double negation errors, or mishandling 'not', 'no', 'never', 'none', 'without' and similar negation markers.
codes.when_to_use: Use when negation is explicitly present in claim or evidence but is ignored, reversed, or incorrectly scoped. Use when 'not X' is treated as 'X' or vice versa. Use when double negation is mishandled.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for temporal 'never' errors (use C.8). Do not use for universal quantifiers like 'none' when the error is about quantification rather than negation (use C.2).
